name: Hymenolepis nana

taxonomy.rank_note: Reference groups can include multiple species. Protozoan higher-rank systems differ; the lineage is provided without forcing every clade into a class rank.

morphology: Egg: 30–50 µm, colorless, with outer membrane, inner embryophore, six-hooked embryo and polar filaments.
Adults are small intestinal tapeworms; internal autoinfection can sustain infection.

transmission.detail: Ingested embryonated eggs can complete a direct cycle through intestinal villi; an optional arthropod intermediate host can carry cysticercoids.

life_cycle.detail: Ingested embryonated eggs can complete a direct cycle through intestinal villi; an optional arthropod intermediate host can carry cysticercoids.

hosts: Definitive: humans and rodents. Intermediate arthropods are optional.
distribution: Worldwide, particularly children and crowded settings; present in tropical regions.
clinical_significance: Heavy infection can cause abdominal pain, diarrhea and reduced appetite; lighter infections may be silent.
diagnostics: Concentrated wet mount at 400× to resolve polar filaments; assess several focal planes.
differential_diagnosis: H. diminuta eggs are larger and lack polar filaments; debris can obscure filaments in poor-quality images.
review_status: Source-compiled educational content; not independently clinically validated

annotation_guidance: Record specimen, stage, stain, objective/total magnification, pixel calibration, source image and reviewer certainty.
Native crops of 200–650 pixels do not determine biological size. Retain µm-per-pixel calibration before resizing.
Split training, validation and test data by patient/specimen; keep related crops in the same split.
Keep damaged or ambiguous objects uncertain. Molecular confirmation of a mixed specimen does not assign every pictured object a species.
